question: According to ______ of the Constitution of India, the President has the power to promulgate Ordinances.
solution:
The correct answer is **__123.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__****

__
 
• Article 123:
 
• of the Indian constitution empowers the President to promulgate ordinances during recess of Parliament(when both the house of the parliament is not in session).
 
 
• The ordinance making power of the President is considered as the most important legislative power of the President.
 
• The ordinance must be approved by the parliament within six weeks of the reassembly.
 
• The maximum life of an ordinance is limited to six months and six weeks.
 
• President can withdraw an ordinance at any time
 
• President can issue an ordinance for only those matters on which Parliament can make laws.
 
• Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed issued the most number of ordinances in India.
 
• The Governor of a state can issue ordinances under Article 213 of the Indian constitution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The President of India is empowered to proclaim three types of emergencies under Article 352, Article 356, Article 360.
 
• Article 72 deals with the pardoning power of the president.
 
• Article 111 deals with the veto power of the president.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 121 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• It mentions the restriction on the discussion in Parliament.
 
• It states that no discussion shall take place in Parliament with respect to the conduct of any Judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court in the discharge of his duties except upon a motion for presenting an address to the President praying for the removal of the Judge as hereinafter provided. 
 
 
 
• **Article 125:**
 
 
• It deals with the Salaries and **others of Judges.**
 
• **It further states**: There shall be paid to the Judges of the Supreme Court such salaries as may be determined by Parliament by law and, until provision in that behalf is so made, such salaries as are specified in the Second Schedule.
 
 
 
• **Article 127:**
 
 
• It deals with the appointment of ad-hoc judges.
 
• Adhoc judges are appointed by the chief justice of India in constitution with the president of India.
 
• The retired judges of the supreme court can be appointed as Adhoc judges but they are not deemed to be judges.
